scope: At the rendered 320x800 discovery page, hold every /api/showtimes response for the initial date, change to the next date, then select the second cinema and wait for both newer query responses. Release an old-date response last and assert the selected date/cinema, current showtime card and role=status count remain for the latest filters.

fixtures.initialDateSource: Captured from the first showtime request; all requests for that date are held to tolerate React StrictMode's development effect replay.

guardInspected: frontend/src/App.tsx showtime effect cleanup sets alive=false. Its then, catch and finally handlers update React state only while alive, preventing a response from a prior filter effect from replacing current state.
environment: Existing local Vite frontend at http://127.0.0.1:5173; Playwright route mocks intercept all API requests; no backend, Docker, database or external service used.

chromiumDesktopMobile.command: $env:GITHUB_ACTIONS='true'; $env:E2E_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:5173'; Remove-Item Env:PLAYWRIGHT_CROSS_BROWSER_SMOKE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; npx playwright test tests/e2e/a11y-states.spec.ts --grep 'TC-E2E-37'

reportNote: A final local rerun passed Chromium desktop/mobile 2/2 in 9.2 seconds and Firefox/WebKit 2/2 in 14.3 seconds. Each Playwright command printed its per-project console result. The JSON and HTML reporter outputs were overwritten by the final Firefox/WebKit command and therefore contain only that project group; successful runs produced no failure trace or screenshot.
limitations: This covers stale successful showtime responses while changing date and cinema filters; stale network errors are not separately tested.
The fixture validates front-end response ordering and rendered DOM/status behavior, not backend query correctness or real screen-reader speech.
Exact-source CI for TC-E2E-37 is pending.
